title: Can a personality test determine if you’re a good fit for a job? With Fred Oswald, PhD

sentences.en: Have you applied for a job lately?
sentences.zh: 你最近申请过工作吗？

sentences.en: If so, you may have been surprised to find that a resume and cover letter weren't enough to get you in the door.
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，你可能会惊讶地发现，仅凭简历和求职信已经不足以让你获得面试机会了。

sentences.en: In addition to these traditional methods of screening job applicants, many companies now also use some form of pre-employment testing,
sentences.zh: 除了这些传统的求职者筛选方式外，许多公司现在还会采用某种形式的入职前测试，

sentences.en: including personality assessments, to help determine whether a candidate will be a good fit for the job.
sentences.zh: 包括性格评估，以帮助确定候选人是否适合该职位。

sentences.en: In fact, one 2018 survey of human resources professionals found that 79% of them use some kind of testing when making external hiring decisions
sentences.zh: 事实上，2018年一项针对人力资源专业人士的调查发现，79%的受访者在做出外部招聘决策时会使用某种测试，

sentences.en: and 72% use testing for internal hires.
sentences.zh: 而72%的受访者在内部招聘时也会使用测试。

sentences.en: So even if you've been in your job for a while, you may find yourself taking an assessment at work.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使你已经在现在的岗位上工作了一段时间，也可能会发现自己在工作中需要参加评估。

sentences.en: The same survey found that 79% of respondents used assessments in their company's career development prograMs.
sentences.zh: 同一项调查还发现，79%的受访者在公司的职业发展项目中使用了评估工具。

sentences.en: So why do employers use these tests?
sentences.zh: 那么，雇主为什么要使用这些测试呢？

sentences.en: Are the assessments that they're using reliable and valid?
sentences.zh: 他们所使用的评估工具可靠且有效吗？

sentences.en: Can a person's personality or other characteristics help predict whether they'll succeed at work?
sentences.zh: 一个人的性格或其他特征能否有助于预测他们未来在工作中的表现？

sentences.en: And how are new technologies, including artificial intelligence, changing workplace assessments?
sentences.zh: 包括人工智能在内的新技术又是如何改变职场评估的呢？

sentences.en: What can employers, employees, and job applicants expect to see next on this front?
sentences.zh: 对于雇主、员工和求职者来说，在这方面接下来会有什么新变化？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Fred Oswald, a professor of industrial organizational psychology and director of the Organization and Workforce Laboratory at Rice University.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是弗雷德·奥斯瓦尔德博士，他是莱斯大学工业与组织心理学教授，也是组织与劳动力实验室的主任。

sentences.en: Dr. Oswald studies the factors that contribute to workplace success, including how to understand, define, and measure the individual differences that affect employees' performance.
sentences.zh: 奥斯瓦尔德博士研究促成职场成功的因素，包括如何理解、定义和衡量影响员工绩效的个体差异。

sentences.en: He's also interested more broadly in the future of work.
sentences.zh: 他还更广泛地关注未来的工作形态。

sentences.en: His 2019 book, Workforce Readiness and the Future of Work, examines how technology, education, and policy will shape the future of work.
sentences.zh: 他2019年出版的著作《劳动力准备与未来工作》探讨了技术、教育和政策将如何塑造未来的工作。

sentences.en: He is a past president of the Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology, which is a division of the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 他曾任美国心理学会下属的工业与组织心理学学会主席。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Oswald.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，奥斯瓦尔德博士。

sentences.en: Kim, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 金，谢谢你的邀请。

sentences.en: This is a real pleasure and I look forward to the conversation today.
sentences.zh: 非常荣幸，我很期待今天的谈话。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Well, let's start with a broad question.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从一个宏观的问题开始。

sentences.en: Why do employers use pre-employment testing?
sentences.zh: 雇主为什么要进行入职前测试？

sentences.en: What do they hope to learn about job applicants that they can't get from a resume, a cover letter, or a job interview?
sentences.zh: 他们希望从求职者身上了解到哪些简历、求职信或面试中无法获取的信息？

sentences.en: Well, testing has a long history and a wide range of purposes, whether we're talking about employment or we all have taken plenty of tests in school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，测试有着悠久的历史和广泛的用途，无论是在就业领域，还是我们每个人在学校里都参加过大量的考试。

sentences.en: There are tests for certification.
sentences.zh: 比如有资格认证考试。

sentences.en: For example, airline pilots take tests to ultimately guard public safety.
sentences.zh: 例如，航空公司飞行员需要参加考试，最终目的是为了保障公共安全。

sentences.en: And employers are hoping to understand who is coming into the workplace.
sentences.zh: 雇主希望了解进入职场的人是谁。

sentences.en: What are their background characteristics?
sentences.zh: 他们的背景特征是什么？

sentences.en: What are the knowledge, skills, and abilities they have coming in?
sentences.zh: 他们具备什么样的知识、技能和能力？

sentences.en: Or what are their qualities?
sentences.zh: 或者他们的素质如何？

sentences.en: I realize we'll talk about personality today.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们今天会谈到性格测试。

sentences.en: And so testing is not perfect, but perfect should not be the enemy of the good in terms
sentences.zh: 测试并不完美，但就使用能够帮助做出正确决策的工具而言，我们不应因追求完美而否定其价值，

sentences.en: of using tools that can help make good decisions, both for the organization and for the job applicant
sentences.zh: 这些决策不仅对组织有利，对求职者也同样重要，

sentences.en: who obviously seeks to find employment that's fitting for them, not merely get an invitation to join the organization, but actually succeed in it.
sentences.zh: 因为求职者显然不仅是想获得一份工作邀请，更是希望能找到适合自己的岗位，并在其中取得成功。

sentences.en: So a moment ago, I mentioned that employers are using testing to make hiring decisions and companies use them in leadership and career development prograMs.
sentences.zh: 刚才我提到，雇主使用测试来做出招聘决策，公司也会在领导力和职业发展项目中使用这些测试。

sentences.en: What kinds of tests are they using?
sentences.zh: 他们具体在使用什么样的测试呢？

sentences.en: What are the questions that employees and prospective employees are being asked?
sentences.zh: 员工和潜在员工会被问到哪些问题？

sentences.en: Yeah, so my own research and experience deals more with personnel selection on the point of initial hire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我个人的研究和经验更多涉及初次招聘时的员工甄选。

sentences.en: So think about characteristics like personality or job knowledge or sometimes logical reasoning skills.
sentences.zh: 所以可以考虑性格、工作知识或逻辑推理能力等特征。

sentences.en: If they don't have, you know, prior background indicated in their resume that they have prior technical skills, there might be a test for some general reasoning.
sentences.zh: 如果简历中没有体现他们具备相关的技术背景，可能就会有针对一般推理能力的测试。

sentences.en: Also, interests and motivation, those obviously differ between people and people have different profiles of interests and types of motivation and goals.
sentences.zh: 此外，兴趣和动机在人与人之间显然存在差异，每个人都有不同的兴趣倾向、动机类型和目标。

sentences.en: And so tests attempt to get at some of those characteristics of job applicants, hopefully in a reliable and valid way.
sentences.zh: 因此，测试试图以一种可靠且有效的方式来捕捉求职者的这些特征。

sentences.en: And we can talk about that further.
sentences.zh: 我们可以进一步讨论这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I did want to talk about that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实想谈谈这个。

sentences.en: And what's the difference between a good workplace assessment tool and a bad one?
sentences.zh: 那么，好的职场评估工具和坏的工具有什么区别？

sentences.en: A useful framework to go off of is think of a three-legged stool of reliability, validity, and fairness.
sentences.zh: 一个有用的参考框架是将其想象成一个三脚凳，即可靠性、有效性和公平性。

sentences.en: Reliability deals with whether what you're measuring is stable over time in the case of job applicants.
sentences.zh: 可靠性是指对于求职者而言，你所测量的内容是否随时间保持稳定。

sentences.en: In other words, you don't want an applicant to be taking a test that is essentially the roll of the dice or is measuring something like mood that fluctuates.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你不希望求职者参加的测试本质上是在掷骰子，或者是在测量情绪这种波动性的东西。

sentences.en: Instead, what you want are characteristics that are likely to appear on the job upon the point of hire.
sentences.zh: 相反，你想要的是那些在入职时很可能在工作中表现出来的特征。

sentences.en: And that's where the employee and the organization starts out with the employee to move them forward through training and development.
sentences.zh: 这就是员工和组织开始合作的起点，通过培训和发展来推动员工成长。

sentences.en: And as you mentioned, leadership and career progression as well.
sentences.zh: 正如你提到的，还有领导力和职业晋升方面。

sentences.en: And so reliability is a cornerstone of measurement to make sure that a test that claims to measure personality, for instance, actually is doing so.
sentences.zh: 因此，可靠性是测量的基石，以确保一个声称测量性格的测试确实做到了这一点。

sentences.en: We could put labels on any test and make the claim that it's measuring what we say.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在任何测试上贴标签，并声称它测量了我们所说的内容。

sentences.en: But how do we know?
sentences.zh: 但我们怎么知道呢？

sentences.en: And we need data to inform that.
sentences.zh: 我们需要数据来提供依据。

sentences.en: And so there are data-based approaches to ensure that scores are measuring what they should.
sentences.zh: 因此，有基于数据的方法来确保分数测量的是它们应该测量的内容。

sentences.en: You know, personality, job knowledge, motivation, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 比如性格、工作知识、动机等等。

sentences.en: And also turning to the second leg of the stool of validity.
sentences.zh: 接下来谈谈三脚凳的第二条腿：有效性。

sentences.en: So do these tests predict outcomes in organizations that we think they should?
sentences.zh: 这些测试是否能预测我们认为它们应该预测的组织成果？

sentences.en: So we know that, for example, conscientiousness is a factor of personality known to predict job performance pretty consistently
sentences.zh: 我们知道，例如，尽责性是一种公认的能够相当稳定地预测工作绩效的性格因素，

sentences.en: over, across jobs, over time, across cultures.
sentences.zh: 无论是在不同工作、不同时间还是不同文化背景下。

sentences.en: And, of course, that relationship makes sense to some degree.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种关系在某种程度上是有道理的。

sentences.en: You need to show up on time for your job.
sentences.zh: 你需要按时上班。

sentences.en: You need to follow the rules.
sentences.zh: 你需要遵守规则。

sentences.en: You need to set goals and achieve them and so on.
sentences.zh: 你需要设定目标并实现它们，等等。

sentences.en: But, like most things in psychology, the devil is in the details.
sentences.zh: 但是，像心理学中的大多数事物一样，魔鬼藏在细节中。

sentences.en: Can you support that common sense with well-developed measures, with evidence, and with good measures behind the data that you're collecting?
sentences.zh: 你能用完善的测量方法、证据以及支撑所收集数据的高质量测量工具来支持这种常识吗？

sentences.en: So not just on the personality side in the case of this example, but how are we measuring performance in the organization?
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅是在性格方面，在组织中我们该如何衡量绩效？

sentences.en: What does it mean to be a successful worker?
sentences.zh: 什么才算是一名成功的员工？

sentences.en: However, it's as much philosophical as it is a measurement and a statistical issue to try and figure out what problem we're trying to solve through testing.
sentences.zh: 然而，试图弄清楚我们通过测试试图解决什么问题，这既是一个哲学问题，也是一个测量和统计学问题。

sentences.en: And then the third leg of the stool is fairness, to make sure that anyone who takes the test has the same opportunities to reflect who they are or what they know.
sentences.zh: 最后，三脚凳的第三条腿是公平性，即确保任何参加测试的人都有平等的机会来反映他们是谁或他们知道什么。

sentences.en: And job irrelevant characteristics are suppressed.
sentences.zh: 并且与工作无关的特征会被剔除。

sentences.en: So, you know, you wouldn't want to test that had too high of a vocabulary level if you're not measuring vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你不是在测量词汇量，你肯定不想使用词汇水平要求过高的测试。

sentences.en: That would be unfair.
sentences.zh: 那是不公平的。

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就是这类事情。

sentences.en: Or accommodating people who have a vision impairment, for example.
sentences.zh: 或者比如为视力受损的人士提供便利。

sentences.en: If visual acuity is not required for the job, then you shouldn't place visual demands on the test for people that need that accommodation.
sentences.zh: 如果工作不需要视敏度，那么就不应该对需要这种便利的人在测试中提出视觉要求。

sentences.en: So being sensitive to the people who are taking tests is just as important as what you do with the scores that come out.
sentences.zh: 因此，对参加测试的人保持敏感，与如何处理测试结果同样重要。

sentences.en: Is there any independent body that validates these tests?
sentences.zh: 是否有任何独立的机构来验证这些测试？

sentences.en: I mean, how would an employer choose one and know that it's a good one?
sentences.zh: 我是说，雇主该如何选择并确保它是有效的呢？

sentences.en: So there are various professional documents that are used by folks who develop tests.
sentences.zh: 有一些专业的文档是供测试开发人员使用的。

sentences.en: So in my world, for example, as you mentioned, I'm a member of the Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology, which is Division 14 within APA.
sentences.zh: 在我的领域，正如你提到的，我是工业与组织心理学会的成员，这是美国心理学会（APA）下的第14分会。

sentences.en: We have a document called the Principles for the Validation and Use of Personnel Selection Procedures.
sentences.zh: 我们有一份名为《人员甄选程序验证与使用原则》的文档。

sentences.en: It's in its fifth edition.
sentences.zh: 目前已经是第五版了。

sentences.en: It's actually free to download through the APA website.
sentences.zh: 它实际上可以在APA网站上免费下载。

sentences.en: And it contains some of the principles that I've reflected on in terms of reliability, validity, and fairness, because those are the principles that go into any test,
sentences.zh: 它包含了我所反思的一些关于信度、效度和公平性的原则，因为这些是任何测试都必须遵循的原则，

sentences.en: no matter what you're measuring, how you're measuring it.
sentences.zh: 无论你在测量什么，或者如何测量。

sentences.en: And, you know, as we move forward into the world of AI and new technologies for measurement,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，随着我们迈向人工智能和新的测量技术时代，

sentences.en: these principles still hold to make sure we're measuring job-relevant characteristics and administering tests in a reliable, fair, valid, secure, ethical, legal manner.
sentences.zh: 这些原则依然适用，以确保我们测量的是与工作相关的特征，并以可靠、公平、有效、安全、合乎道德且合法的方式进行测试。

sentences.en: And so that's a major resource in the area of employment testing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是就业测试领域的一项重要资源。

sentences.en: But there's also the Standards for Educational and Psychological Assessment, which APA is also involved in as a co-editor with two other organizations.
sentences.zh: 但还有《教育与心理评估标准》，APA也作为联合编辑与其他两个组织共同参与了该标准。

sentences.en: And similar principles apply, but it's broadened into the domains, as the title suggests, into education, whether that's K-12 or, you know,
sentences.zh: 适用的原则类似，但正如标题所示，其领域已扩展到教育，无论是K-12还是，你知道，

sentences.en: placement issues into different educational prograMs.
sentences.zh: 针对不同教育项目的安置问题。

sentences.en: And it's more about that context.
sentences.zh: 它更多是关于那种背景。

sentences.en: So hopefully those who are listening understand that, you know, we've been thinking about tests for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以希望听众们能理解，你知道，我们对测试的研究已经很久了。

sentences.en: The SAP document, the SAP document I mentioned, it's in its fifth edition, it's maybe as many decades old or close to it.
sentences.zh: 我提到的那个SAP文档，现在是第五版，可能已经有几十年历史了，或者差不多。

sentences.en: And so serious attention has been paid to help ensure that tests are measuring what they should.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们非常关注如何确保测试能够测量到它们应该测量的东西。

sentences.en: And anyone seeking to purchase a test should be thinking about some of these issues, or at least they would benefit from doing so,
sentences.zh: 任何想要购买测试的人都应该考虑这些问题，或者至少这样做会让他们受益，

sentences.en: and not merely trusting what they, what sounds good, but actually seeing whether there's evidence behind the claims of a test being reliable, valid, and fair.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅相信那些听起来不错的东西，而是要真正看看是否有证据支持该测试在信度、效度和公平性方面的声明。

sentences.en: One of the reasons that I wanted to talk to you today was because of a kerfuffle that ensued among some psychologists a couple of months ago
sentences.zh: 我今天想和你谈谈的原因之一，是因为几个月前心理学家之间发生了一场小风波，

sentences.en: when HBO Max aired a documentary film called Persona, The Dark Truth Behind Personality Tests.
sentences.zh: 当时HBO Max播出了一部名为《人格：人格测试背后的黑暗真相》的纪录片。

sentences.en: The film focused mostly on the Myers-Briggs personality test, which I'm sure a lot of our listeners have heard of and maybe have even taken.
sentences.zh: 这部电影主要关注迈尔斯-布里格斯类型指标（MBTI），我相信我们的很多听众都听说过，甚至可能做过。

sentences.en: What's your view of this test in particular?
sentences.zh: 你对这个测试有什么看法？

sentences.en: Is it a valid tool for employers and why is it so popular?
sentences.zh: 它对雇主来说是一个有效的工具吗？为什么它如此受欢迎？

sentences.en: I'm hesitating here because I don't want to put any particular company test on the mat or as a target, but we all understand that the Myers-Briggs is a popular teSt.
sentences.zh: 我在这里犹豫是因为我不想把任何特定的公司测试放在审判台上或作为攻击目标，但我们都知道迈尔斯-布里格斯是一个很受欢迎的测试。

sentences.en: It's used widely in organizations for a variety of purposes.
sentences.zh: 它在组织中被广泛用于各种目的。

sentences.en: And what I'll say about that test really applies more generally to tests that are like it.
sentences.zh: 我对此测试的评价实际上更适用于类似的测试。

sentences.en: The early versions of the Myers-Briggs, and I realize the test has been revised, perhaps in ways I'm unaware of,
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯-布里格斯的早期版本——我知道该测试已经过修订，也许是以我不知道的方式——

sentences.en: but at least the fundamentals of the test in its early development had to do with profiles.
sentences.zh: 但至少该测试在早期开发中的基本原理与“画像”有关。

sentences.en: So a person would say they are an INTJ, and I honestly forget what that stands for, but it's something like introverted and thinking and judgmental, things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以一个人会说他们是INTJ，我老实说忘了这代表什么，但大概是内向、思考和判断之类的意思。

sentences.en: And so the profile is used to intuitive, sorry, I'm going back to the end there, introverted, intuitive, thinking, and judging.
sentences.zh: 所以这个画像被用来……抱歉，我回到最后那个词，是内向、直觉、思考和判断。

sentences.en: But the point of that is to say that profiles are a complex way of describing a person,
sentences.zh: 但重点是，画像是一种描述人的复杂方式，

sentences.en: and what you could ask before turning to profiles is whether the single variables that are part of that profile,
sentences.zh: 而在转向画像之前，你可以问的是，作为画像一部分的单一变量，

sentences.en: where do you stand on those characteristics rather than jumping forward to that complex INTJ combination?
sentences.zh: 你在这些特征上处于什么位置，而不是直接跳到那个复杂的INTJ组合？

sentences.en: Because science prefers simplicity before you jump into complexity.
sentences.zh: 因为科学在进入复杂性之前更倾向于简单性。

sentences.en: So in other words, a researcher would look at INTJ and break those variables apart and see how those variables, intuitive, introverted, thinking, judging,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，研究人员会观察INTJ并拆解这些变量，看看这些变量——直觉、内向、思考、判断——

sentences.en: how those correlate with each other and how they correlate with organizational outcomes.
sentences.zh: 它们之间如何相关，以及它们如何与组织成果相关联。

sentences.en: See what those relationships are, and then see if a profile or something complicated like that predicts above and beyond the more straightforward relationships.
sentences.zh: 看看这些关系是什么，然后看看像画像这样复杂的东西是否比更直接的关系具有更好的预测力。

sentences.en: So I think that's where the general arguments lie around the test is that it's not clear whether the profiles add anything above and beyond a traditional test
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是围绕该测试的主要争议所在，即不清楚这些画像是否比传统测试增加了任何额外价值，

sentences.en: that is more transparent and straightforward in terms of how it's measuring personality traits rather than combining those traits into profiles.
sentences.zh: 那种在测量人格特质时更透明、更直接，而不是将这些特质组合成画像的测试。

sentences.en: I will say that the profiles do lead to interesting conversations and perhaps yield interesting and useful insights.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这些画像确实能引发有趣的对话，或许也能产生有趣且有用的见解。

sentences.en: But whether those conversations and insights actually have an impact in terms of, you know, if you took the test for leader development,
sentences.zh: 但这些对话和见解是否真的有影响，比如，如果你为了领导力发展而参加了测试，

sentences.en: would it help you in terms of your job success?
sentences.zh: 它能帮助你获得工作上的成功吗？

sentences.en: I think the evidence is not as strong as it is for more tests in the more traditional vein that I mentioned, measuring one trait at a time.
sentences.zh: 我认为证据不如我提到的那些更传统的测试强，即一次测量一个特质的测试。

sentences.en: So many of the validated tests that are being used in the workplace are based on what's called the big five personality traits.
sentences.zh: 所以许多在工作场所使用的经过验证的测试都是基于所谓的“大五人格特质”。

sentences.en: Some of our listeners may know what they are, but could you explain what the big five are and the history of that model of personality?
sentences.zh: 我们的一些听众可能知道它们是什么，但你能解释一下什么是“大五”以及该人格模型的历史吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So briefly, and this reflects on the point of measuring one trait at a time, the big five measures, as the name implies, five traits.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，这反映了刚才提到的“一次测量一个特质”的观点，“大五”正如其名，测量五个特质。

sentences.en: So conscientiousness is one that I had mentioned already.
sentences.zh: 尽责性是我之前提到过的一个。

sentences.en: There's extroversion, agreeableness, openness, and neuroticism, which is an unfortunate term because all the traits are intended to measure normal personality.
sentences.zh: 还有外向性、宜人性、开放性和神经质，这是一个不幸的术语，因为所有这些特质都是为了测量正常人格。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean you're neurotic if you score highly, but it does mean that there's a distribution that people have in terms of their anxiety and worry, things like that.
sentences.zh: 得分高并不意味着你神经质，但确实意味着人们在焦虑和担忧等方面存在分布差异，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Again, within the normal range.
sentences.zh: 同样，是在正常范围内。

sentences.en: Same thing for all the other traits.
sentences.zh: 所有其他特质也是如此。

sentences.en: If you're low on conscientiousness, that doesn't mean you're abysmally low.
sentences.zh: 如果你在尽责性上得分低，那并不意味着你低得离谱。

sentences.en: It just means you're low relative to other people.
sentences.zh: 只是意味着相对于其他人来说你比较低。

sentences.en: And same for the other traits that are being measured.
sentences.zh: 其他被测量的特质也是如此。

sentences.en: These are all in the normal range.
sentences.zh: 这些都在正常范围内。

sentences.en: These are not clinical measures of personality.
sentences.zh: 这些不是临床人格测量。

sentences.en: And so how those factors were derived is actually from the dictionary.
sentences.zh: 这些因素实际上是从字典中推导出来的。

sentences.en: So some folks early in the history of personality psychology scoured the dictionary for these descriptive terms for people
sentences.zh: 所以人格心理学史上的一些早期研究者在字典中搜寻这些描述人的词汇，

sentences.en: and essentially gave those terms as a test, asking people, how much do these terms apply to you?
sentences.zh: 并基本上把这些词汇作为测试题目，询问人们：这些词汇在多大程度上适用于你？

sentences.en: And there were various rules for which words got included and excluded and so on.
sentences.zh: 对于哪些词被包含或排除等，有各种各样的规则。

sentences.en: But the point is they gave this test and then they looked at the themes.
sentences.zh: 但重点是他们进行了这项测试，然后观察其中的主题。

sentences.en: They used statistics to find these factors, these underlying themes that basically cluster the types of responses people were making.
sentences.zh: 他们利用统计学找到了这些因素，即那些基本上将人们的反应类型进行聚类的潜在主题。

sentences.en: And there were five clusters.
sentences.zh: 总共有五个聚类。

sentences.en: Hence the big five came out of that.
sentences.zh: 因此，“大五”就是由此产生的。

sentences.en: And so psychologists will talk about the lexical hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 心理学家们会谈到词汇假设。

sentences.en: And that refers to this dictionary, the lexicon, dictionary-based approach to deriving personality.
sentences.zh: 这指的是那种基于词典、基于词汇的方法，用来推导人格特征。

sentences.en: There are variations on the big five.
sentences.zh: “大五人格”模型也有一些变体。

sentences.en: For example, the Hexaco model is there are nuances that make it more different than the big five, than simply adding a sixth factor.
sentences.zh: 例如，HEXACO模型，它与大五人格之间存在一些细微差别，不仅仅是增加了一个第六维度。

sentences.en: But I will say that one distinction, one big distinction, is a sixth factor called honesty and humility, the HH factor, honesty, humility.
sentences.zh: 但我得说，其中一个重要的区别是增加了一个被称为“诚实-谦逊”的第六维度，即HH维度。

sentences.en: And that factor proves to be useful in measuring personality and understanding employees.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这一维度在衡量人格和了解员工方面非常有用。

sentences.en: There are organizations that will give so-called integrity tests that they find from test vendors.
sentences.zh: 有些组织会使用从测试供应商那里获得的所谓“诚信测试”。

sentences.en: And those tests are asking questions about the typical behaviors someone exhibits that are, again, these are in the normal range.
sentences.zh: 这些测试询问的是一个人在正常范围内所表现出的典型行为。

sentences.en: But, you know, what are described as your workplace behaviors in terms of honesty and integrity.
sentences.zh: 也就是在诚实和正直方面，你被描述出的职场行为。

sentences.en: So it sounds like those five or six terms that we were talking about, that those can be fairly reliably predicted then based on testing?
sentences.zh: 听起来我们刚才讨论的那五六个维度，通过测试就能相当可靠地预测出来？

sentences.en: Yeah, that people can write, the folks who are developing personality tests can write items under each of the big five that reflect reliability and validity
sentences.zh: 是的，人们可以编写测试题，那些开发人格测试的人可以在大五人格的每个维度下编写反映可靠性和有效性的题目，

sentences.en: and can write them in a way that is accessible to people and fair in that sense.
sentences.zh: 并且以一种人们易于理解且公平的方式来编写。

sentences.en: They do vary in terms of their validity.
sentences.zh: 它们的有效性确实各不相同。

sentences.en: So conscientiousness is probably the most valid of those five traits, just focusing within personality testing.
sentences.zh: 就人格测试而言，尽责性可能是这五个特质中最有效的一个。

sentences.en: But there is continued research on facets of personality.
sentences.zh: 但关于人格侧面的研究仍在继续。

sentences.en: So facets are the kind of sub-factors that underlie the big five.
sentences.zh: 侧面是指构成大五人格的子维度。

sentences.en: They focus on narrower aspects of personality.
sentences.zh: 它们关注的是人格中更狭窄的方面。

sentences.en: So, for example, under the factor of conscientiousness, you might think about whether somebody is being more kind of achievement striving,
sentences.zh: 例如，在尽责性这一维度下，你可以考虑某人是否更倾向于追求成就，

sentences.en: like it's kind of a moving forward motion of setting your goals and following through,
sentences.zh: 就像设定目标并坚持到底的那种前进动力，

sentences.en: versus a rule following notion, being dutiful or maintaining order or paying attention to detail.
sentences.zh: 还是倾向于遵守规则，比如尽职尽责、维持秩序或注重细节。

sentences.en: That's more of a kind of a tediousness to it, right?
sentences.zh: 那更多是一种枯燥感，对吧？

sentences.en: It's more kind of inward focus as opposed to outward focus.
sentences.zh: 它更多是一种内在的关注，而不是外在的关注。

sentences.en: So there are these facets that can be measured reliably and that perhaps have different relationships with organizational outcomes than those broader factors.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些侧面可以被可靠地测量，而且它们与组织成果的关系可能与那些更广泛的维度不同。

sentences.en: Is it possible for applicants to game these tests?
sentences.zh: 求职者有可能在这些测试中作弊吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I imagine that some of these questions are not so obvious and not going to ask you, are you an honest person?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想象其中一些问题并不那么明显，也不会直接问你“你是一个诚实的人吗？”

sentences.en: But can applicants figure out a way to give the employer an answer that would get them in the door for the interview, but it may not even be true?
sentences.zh: 但求职者能否找到一种方法，给雇主一个能让他们获得面试机会的答案，即使那可能不是真实的？

sentences.en: Yeah, there's no doubt that people can lie on personality tests.
sentences.zh: 是的，毫无疑问，人们在人格测试中是可以撒谎的。

sentences.en: And so if everybody did so, then we would throw the tests out the window that there's nothing that will help in terms of being reliable or valid.
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都这么做，那我们就会把这些测试扔进垃圾桶，因为它们在可靠性或有效性方面就毫无帮助了。

sentences.en: But it turns out people, you know, while some people do lie, and as I mentioned,
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，虽然有些人确实会撒谎，正如我提到的，

sentences.en: the perfect shouldn't be the enemy of the good because there's enough variation in responses that is reliable that can be used for understanding the employee.
sentences.zh: 完美不应成为优秀的敌人，因为回复中存在足够多的可靠变异，可以用来了解员工。

sentences.en: And again, you know, these questions are trying to get at normal personality.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这些问题试图触及的是正常人格。

sentences.en: The framing of the framing of the test is to indicate who you are and that, you know, it doesn't necessarily serve you well to lie on the teSt.
sentences.zh: 测试的框架是为了表明你是谁，而且，你知道，在测试中撒谎并不一定对你有好处。

sentences.en: Some tests actually attempt forms of lie detection to see if you're just, you know, kind of responding on the fly without thinking carefully through the iteMs.
sentences.zh: 有些测试实际上会尝试进行某种形式的测谎，看看你是否只是在没有仔细思考题目的情况下随手作答。

sentences.en: There are various methods for that.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Those aren't perfect either.
sentences.zh: 这些方法也不完美。

sentences.en: But again, the goal is to try and find a good fit between the job applicant and the employer.
sentences.zh: 但同样，目标是试图在求职者和雇主之间找到一个良好的匹配。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the straightforward answer to your question is people certainly can lie.
sentences.zh: 所以，对你问题的直接回答是，人们当然可以撒谎。

sentences.en: But in the context of real-world personality testing,
sentences.zh: 但在现实世界的人格测试背景下，

sentences.en: we don't see that to the extent that we would throw away personality tests as part of the employment kind of battery of tests we would administer.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有看到那种程度的撒谎，以至于我们要把人格测试从我们使用的雇佣测试组合中剔除。

sentences.en: I think you mentioned integrity tests, you know, an item might be something like,
sentences.zh: 我想你提到了诚信测试，你知道，题目可能是这样的：

sentences.en: I would turn in a fellow worker I saw stealing money or an employee should be fired if the employer finds out the employee lied on their job application.
sentences.zh: “如果我看到同事偷钱，我会举报他”或者“如果雇主发现员工在求职申请中撒谎，该员工就应该被解雇”。

sentences.en: And, you know, those items may have right or wrong answers, but there are degrees of how much you might endorse it.
sentences.zh: 这些题目可能有对错之分，但你对它的认同程度是有等级的。

sentences.en: So the format might be on, say, a one to five scale rather than true or false.
sentences.zh: 所以形式可能是1到5分的量表，而不是简单的对或错。

sentences.en: And that provides enough variation to be able to get some reliable differences between people and their standing on a personality trait.
sentences.zh: 这提供了足够的变异，能够得出人们在人格特质上的可靠差异。

sentences.en: So one of your research interests is new ways of using technology to measure personality, including big data and artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 你研究的兴趣之一是利用技术来衡量人格的新方法，包括大数据和人工智能。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: I think some of our listeners may have read news stories about companies using AI to interpret applicants' facial expressions during job interviews, for example.
sentences.zh: 我想我们的一些听众可能读过关于公司在面试中使用人工智能来解读求职者面部表情的新闻报道。

sentences.en: So what are the potential advantages of these new technologies and what might be potential pitfalls?
sentences.zh: 那么这些新技术有哪些潜在优势，又有哪些潜在陷阱？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we're talking about the Wild West here.
sentences.zh: 我们现在谈论的是一个“狂野西部”般的领域。

sentences.en: That these AI technologies for selection are developing at the same time that we're thinking about them and safeguarding applicant privacy and judging whether these tests will provide benefit in general and above and beyond traditional tests,
sentences.zh: 这些用于选拔的人工智能技术在发展的同时，我们也在思考它们，保护求职者的隐私，并判断这些测试是否能提供超越传统测试的总体益处，

sentences.en: perhaps.
sentences.zh: 或许吧。

sentences.en: And I think it's important for listeners to appreciate at some level this distinction, several distinctions that are part of AI testing.
sentences.zh: 我认为听众在某种程度上理解人工智能测试中的这种区别，即几个区别，是很重要的。

sentences.en: So the technology is one part of testing.
sentences.zh: 技术只是测试的一部分。

sentences.en: So how are you gathering the data?
sentences.zh: 你是如何收集数据的？

sentences.en: So it could be video, although that has been state legislation has rightfully come up to worry,
sentences.zh: 可能是视频，尽管州立法已经理所当然地提出了担忧，

sentences.en: to express concerns about whether gathering video images of applicants is really a good way of understanding the applicant.
sentences.zh: 表达了对收集求职者视频图像是否真的是了解求职者的好方法的担忧。

sentences.en: And we can talk about that further, if you like, but there's a technology for gathering the job applicants characteristics.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，我们可以进一步讨论，但确实存在一种收集求职者特征的技术。

sentences.en: So those could be audio, the audio could be processing tone, which again might be problematic, but the language, you know,
sentences.zh: 可能是音频，音频可以处理语调，这可能又会有问题，但语言方面，你知道，

sentences.en: trying to extract themes out of what people say and maybe supplement the human interviewer in terms of reminding the interviewer the things that were said and the themes that emerged.
sentences.zh: 试图从人们说的话中提取主题，或许可以辅助人类面试官，提醒面试官所说的事情和出现的主题。

sentences.en: In other words, it could be a hybrid approach rather than pure AI potentially.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这可能是一种混合方法，而不是纯粹的人工智能。

sentences.en: Other technologies are game-based assessment.
sentences.zh: 其他技术是基于游戏的评估。

sentences.en: So we all have probably heard ads like, hey, get online, play this game, and you can see what jobs are right for you.
sentences.zh: 我们可能都听过这样的广告：嘿，上网玩这个游戏，你就能知道什么工作适合你。

sentences.en: And it sounds engaging and fun and data-driven and so on.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很有吸引力、很有趣、数据驱动等等。

sentences.en: But again, the principles of whether the test is reliable, valid, and fair applies there.
sentences.zh: 但同样，测试是否可靠、有效和公平的原则也适用于此。

sentences.en: But they are games.
sentences.zh: 但它们毕竟是游戏。

sentences.en: They're fast to take.
sentences.zh: 它们完成得很快。

sentences.en: They might be fun.
sentences.zh: 它们可能很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, so we're operating in this new world of selection where the standard fill-in-the-bubble tests are maybe increasingly being left behind in light of these new technologies.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正处于这个新的选拔世界中，鉴于这些新技术，标准的“填涂气泡”式测试可能正逐渐被淘汰。

sentences.en: So how do we make those technologies better is where my work kind of stands is I think there's some criticisms to be made, but at the same time,
sentences.zh: 所以我的工作重点在于如何改进这些技术，我认为虽然可以提出一些批评，但同时，

sentences.en: balancing criticisms with opportunities.
sentences.zh: 要在批评与机遇之间取得平衡。

sentences.en: What can we do better?
sentences.zh: 我们能做得更好吗？

sentences.en: How can we move these technologies forward?
sentences.zh: 我们如何推动这些技术向前发展？

sentences.en: Another part of the distinctions that I mentioned to be made is the algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 我提到的另一个区别是算法。

sentences.en: So they're the technologies, and then they're the algorithms that are applied to the data that are collected.
sentences.zh: 有技术，然后有应用于所收集数据的算法。

sentences.en: So how do algorithms provide scores for people that are taking these tests?
sentences.zh: 那么算法是如何为参加这些测试的人提供分数的呢？

sentences.en: So it's one thing for somebody to take a personality test and you add up their score of simple addition.
sentences.zh: 一个人参加人格测试并进行简单的加法计算分数是一回事。

sentences.en: But it's quite another thing to use machine learning, you know,
sentences.zh: 但使用机器学习，你知道，

sentences.en: these sophisticated algorithms onto somebody's behavior as they play a game and try and figure out what themes are in there.
sentences.zh: 将这些复杂的算法应用到某人在玩游戏时的行为上，并试图找出其中的主题，则是另一回事。

sentences.en: So that distinction, I think, is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种区别非常重要。

sentences.en: And related to this is the type of data where some data may appear directly more psychological.
sentences.zh: 与此相关的是数据的类型，有些数据看起来更直接地具有心理学意义。

sentences.en: You know, a game might have you literally answer questions about personality, perhaps, and it would look almost like the test, a traditional teSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个游戏可能会让你直接回答关于人格的问题，它看起来几乎就像传统的测试。

sentences.en: Or you might solve a cognitive puzzle, and it looks exactly like a puzzle you might get on paper in a cognitive test or a knowledge test, right?
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会解决一个认知难题，它看起来就像你在认知测试或知识测试中在纸上看到的难题一样，对吧？

sentences.en: You could be asked about knowledge within a game.
sentences.zh: 你可能会在游戏中被问及知识。

sentences.en: So those are more straightforward and I would say are more intentionally measuring the psychological characteristics of job applicants you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 所以这些更直接，我认为它们更有意地在衡量你感兴趣的求职者的心理特征。

sentences.en: And that's being contrasted with more incidental data.
sentences.zh: 这与更偶然的数据形成了对比。

sentences.en: So incidental means, you know, as you mentioned, the video capture or, you know, learning about maybe there's something in a resume that an AI engine is scraping from the web,
sentences.zh: 偶然意味着，正如你提到的，视频捕捉，或者，你知道，了解简历中可能存在的内容，人工智能引擎从网上抓取，

sentences.en: getting people's resumes and extracting themes from them.
sentences.zh: 获取人们的简历并从中提取主题。

sentences.en: And they're not intentionally expressing the psychological features that might be inferred, but instead it's incidental.
sentences.zh: 它们并不是有意地表达可能被推断出的心理特征，而是偶然的。

sentences.en: It happens to be discovered.
sentences.zh: 它们只是碰巧被发现了。

sentences.en: And those are the promises of AI where we're hoping to discover psychological characteristics from data.
sentences.zh: 这就是人工智能的承诺，我们希望从数据中发现心理特征。

sentences.en: But again, this opportunity also has risk in terms of issues of privacy and ethics, which we all care about.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这种机遇在隐私和道德问题上也存在风险，这是我们大家都关心的。

sentences.en: Not to mention litigation, which organizations care about.
sentences.zh: 更不用说组织所关心的诉讼问题了。

sentences.en: So some of these games that are intended to tell you whether your personality is suited for a particular job, are those really valid?
sentences.zh: 那么，有些旨在告诉你人格是否适合特定工作的游戏，它们真的有效吗？

sentences.en: And what happens, say, if your employer gives you one of these to play when you're already on the job,
sentences.zh: 如果你的雇主在你已经在职时让你玩其中一个游戏，结果会怎样？

sentences.en: and it turns out that you don't have the right makeup for the job that you have?
sentences.zh: 结果发现你并不具备这份工作所需的特质？

sentences.en: Maybe it requires creativity, and the game says, you're a brick, man.
sentences.zh: 也许它需要创造力，而游戏说：“伙计，你就像块砖头一样。”

sentences.en: You're not creative at all.
sentences.zh: 你一点创造力都没有。

sentences.en: What are you doing in this job?
sentences.zh: 你在这份工作中做什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, tests are one part of a larger picture of decision making, or at least they should be treated as such.
sentences.zh: 是的，测试只是决策大局的一部分，或者至少应该被视为如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, how much weight can you put into a game is a good question.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你能在一个游戏中投入多少权重是一个好问题。

sentences.en: Or how much weight can you put into any test?
sentences.zh: 或者你能对任何测试投入多少权重？

sentences.en: You know, speaking to the job applicant situation, if somebody is new to the world of work, they just got out of high school,
sentences.zh: 说到求职者的情况，如果某人是职场新人，刚从高中毕业，

sentences.en: and they're applying for jobs and don't have much work experience.
sentences.zh: 他们正在申请工作，没有多少工作经验。

sentences.en: In that case, tests might be more useful because it's supplying information in a systematic way that doesn't show up in any resume.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，测试可能更有用，因为它以一种系统的方式提供了简历中没有的信息。

sentences.en: And it's sort of the idea that there, you know, there are personality features and knowledge features that suggest the person will be a promising young employee.
sentences.zh: 这是一种理念，即存在一些人格特征和知识特征，表明这个人会成为一名有前途的年轻员工。

sentences.en: By contrast, if somebody has an extensive resume with, you know, expertise being reflected, they're a neurosurgeon, for example,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，如果某人有一份详尽的简历，反映出专业知识，例如他们是一名神经外科医生，

sentences.en: perhaps a game attempting to measure job knowledge is not necessary.
sentences.zh: 也许就不需要通过游戏来衡量工作知识了。

sentences.en: And then there are cases where the test isn't perfect, but it's trying to measure these characteristics that are, you know,
sentences.zh: 还有一些情况，测试并不完美，但它试图衡量这些特征，你知道，

sentences.en: honestly hard to get at through tests or through any other way, like creativity.
sentences.zh: 通过测试或任何其他方式都很难获得，比如创造力。

sentences.en: And so maybe those tests are used for developmental purposes and not for selection necessarily, not for saying you will, you know, have a problem in this job, but rather to say,
sentences.zh: 所以也许这些测试是用于发展目的，而不是必然用于选拔，不是为了说你在这份工作中会有问题，而是为了说，

sentences.en: here's what this game is indicating.
sentences.zh: 这是游戏所显示的内容。

sentences.en: And, you know, as a developmental conversation, how do you see that informing what you should be doing next to work on your creativity?
sentences.zh: 而且，作为一次发展对话，你认为这如何为你接下来应该做些什么来提升创造力提供参考？

sentences.en: And so to the extent those scores have some reliability and validity, then that's a worthwhile conversation because the test is actually diagnosing something about creativity.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这些分数具有一定的可靠性和有效性，那么这是一次有价值的对话，因为测试实际上是在诊断关于创造力的某些东西。

sentences.en: Creativity is a hard thing to measure, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，创造力是一个很难衡量的东西。

sentences.en: It sometimes depends on your prior knowledge.
sentences.zh: 它有时取决于你先前的知识。

sentences.en: So you need to, you know, it's not necessarily open-ended, in other words.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要，你知道，换句话说，它不一定是开放式的。

sentences.en: Some types of creativity are where you just let your mind go and think about whatever pops into mind.
sentences.zh: 有些类型的创造力是你只是让思维发散，思考任何跳入脑海的东西。

sentences.en: But in other cases, it's where, you know,
sentences.zh: 但在其他情况下，你知道，

sentences.en: luck fares the well-prepared in a sense that you have a lot of knowledge in your head and then you're asked to create and you have all these knowledge frameworks that assist in your creativity.
sentences.zh: 运气眷顾有准备的人，从某种意义上说，你脑子里有很多知识，然后你被要求创造，你拥有所有这些辅助你创造的知识框架。

sentences.en: So I will say it from the get-go that that's a tough construct to measure with tests or otherwise.
sentences.zh: 所以我从一开始就会说，这是一个很难用测试或其他方式衡量的构念。

sentences.en: That's a topic that we're going to be exploring in a future podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是我们将在未来的播客中探讨的话题。

sentences.en: So listeners, stay tuned because we will come back and talk to some experts about creativity, which is really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 所以听众们，请保持关注，因为我们会回来和一些专家谈谈创造力，这真的非常迷人。

sentences.en: So what would you say to a job applicant who might be uncomfortable with the idea of an algorithm instead of a person evaluating their job application?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那些对“由算法而不是人来评估求职申请”这一想法感到不舒服的求职者，你会说什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I think, you know, AI is as much a cultural feature as it is technology.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，人工智能既是一种文化特征，也是一种技术。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, we're trying to figure out as researchers and as people who are subjected to these technologies, how is that going to change the world of work?
sentences.zh: 我认为，作为研究人员和作为这些技术的受试者，我们正在试图弄清楚这将如何改变职场世界。

sentences.en: You know, will it be better for employees?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这对员工会更好吗？

sentences.en: Will it be better for organizations?
sentences.zh: 这对组织会更好吗？

sentences.en: How will it work when AI is even more infused into organizations and perhaps becomes a given in how selection happens?
sentences.zh: 当人工智能更深入地融入组织，并可能成为选拔方式中的既定事实时，它将如何运作？

sentences.en: That will be a different world than what we're experiencing today where we don't see – we see the entry point.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个与我们今天所经历的不同的世界，我们现在看到的只是切入点。

sentences.en: We see AI entering the area of selection and continuing to grow.
sentences.zh: 我们看到人工智能进入了选拔领域，并持续增长。

sentences.en: And as this is happening, we do see, you know, those going through those experiences as applicants are clearly talking and probably tweeting and getting a sense of how it works.
sentences.zh: 随着这种情况的发生，我们确实看到，那些作为求职者经历这些过程的人显然在讨论，可能也在发推文，并对它的运作方式有所了解。

sentences.en: You know, state legislation keeps arising in response to these technologies to try and ensure the tests are measuring reliable characteristics of applicants,
sentences.zh: 你知道，州立法不断涌现以应对这些技术，试图确保测试衡量的是求职者可靠的特征，

sentences.en: job-relevant characteristics that are important at the point of selection.
sentences.zh: 即在选拔时重要的、与工作相关的特征。

sentences.en: Not just relevant for the job, but relevant at the point of selection.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是与工作相关，而且是在选拔时相关。

sentences.en: I think that's important to emphasize.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点很重要，需要强调。

sentences.en: I think that's important to emphasize.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点很重要，需要强调。

sentences.en: And not invasive and, you know, legal and ethical and those things.
sentences.zh: 而且不具侵入性，你知道，合法、合乎道德等等。

sentences.en: But the devil is in the details there.
sentences.zh: 但魔鬼藏在细节中。

sentences.en: Reading these state bills or, you know, regulations,
sentences.zh: 阅读这些州法案或，你知道，法规，

sentences.en: the language is open-ended because the technology is still being developed and we need to figure out what are appropriate uses and what are inappropriate uses.
sentences.zh: 语言是开放式的，因为技术仍在开发中，我们需要弄清楚什么是适当的用途，什么是不适当的用途。

sentences.en: You know, video capture seems to be most problematic to try and infer employee characteristics from their feet, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，视频捕捉似乎是最有问题的，试图从他们的表现中推断员工特征，你知道，

sentences.en: how they look or how they – how they're – what the emotions on their face and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们的外表，或者他们——他们——他们脸上的表情等等。

sentences.en: That seems very problematic and is.
sentences.zh: 这看起来非常有问题，而且确实如此。

sentences.en: It's not like the algorithm did detect highly relevant job features and we should be using it.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说算法确实检测到了高度相关的工作特征，我们应该使用它。

sentences.en: There doesn't seem to be evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 似乎没有证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: So, the evidence, lack of evidence is also a concern in that area.
sentences.zh: 所以，证据，缺乏证据也是该领域的一个担忧。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think we will wait and see in terms of how people will – it will evolve, I guess would be my answer.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我想我们会拭目以待，看看人们将如何——它将如何演变，我想这就是我的回答。

sentences.en: Just like self-driving cars, right, have barely happened yet.
sentences.zh: 就像自动驾驶汽车一样，对吧，几乎还没真正实现呢。

sentences.en: There are some very isolated instances of self-driving cars being in the world.
sentences.zh: 目前世界上确实有一些非常零星的自动驾驶汽车应用案例。

sentences.en: But once they become more commonplace, we'll have an entirely different phenomenon on our hands.
sentences.zh: 但一旦它们变得普及，我们将面临一种截然不同的现象。

sentences.en: I think there's also the applicant perceptions of the hiring process that will evolve as much as the decisions that are made from AI will evolve.
sentences.zh: 我认为，随着人工智能所做决策的演变，求职者对招聘流程的看法也会随之发生改变。

sentences.en: So, in other words, as you get more used to AI as a tool for selection, maybe people will see that humans supplementing selection becomes the add-on, the part that's valued,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，随着大家越来越习惯将人工智能作为筛选工具，也许人们会发现，人类对筛选过程的补充反而成了附加值，成了被看重的那部分，

sentences.en: which would, you know, kind of turn the tables on the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上会彻底扭转整个局面。

sentences.en: So, it'll be interesting to see how humans merge with AI as AI permeates selection.
sentences.zh: 所以，观察人工智能如何渗透到筛选过程中，以及人类如何与人工智能融合，将会是一件很有趣的事情。

sentences.en: An applicant might feel that the organization is not paying much attention to them by farming it out to an AI to do selection on a broad scale.
sentences.zh: 求职者可能会觉得，企业通过大规模外包给人工智能进行筛选，是对他们不够重视。

sentences.en: That would be a negative, but a positive could be that AI is treating applicants fairly.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个负面影响，但正面影响在于人工智能对待求职者可能更加公平。

sentences.en: I mean, imagine AI tools that are making every attempt to be fair and accurate in ways that humans try to be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想象一下那些人工智能工具，它们正试图以人类所追求的方式做到公平和准确。

sentences.en: That would be a positive aspect of AI in the future as we continue to develop tools that are effective.
sentences.zh: 随着我们不断开发出有效的工具，这将是人工智能在未来积极的一面。

sentences.en: So, it won't do things like humans do, like prejudge people based on their names, which they're unusual or foreign-sounding.
sentences.zh: 这样它就不会像人类那样，因为求职者的名字听起来不寻常或带有异国情调而产生偏见。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or maybe you make a judgment because, oh, this person went to my alma mater, I'm going to give her an interview.
sentences.zh: 或者，你可能会因为“哦，这个人是我的校友，我要给她一个面试机会”而做出判断。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Those sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 就是这类事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, those sorts of things that, right, we're supposed to be selecting on job-relevant characteristics and not irrelevancies like your name or your background.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是这类事情。没错，我们本应根据与工作相关的特质进行筛选，而不是根据名字或背景这些无关紧要的因素。

sentences.en: And another aspect, I think, to consider is sometimes people think, well, tests are not any better because they're deterministic.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一点需要考虑，有时人们会觉得，测试因为具有确定性，所以并没有更好。

sentences.en: And that's not true either.
sentences.zh: 这也是不对的。

sentences.en: Tests are a way of letting employers know what an applicant looks like.
sentences.zh: 测试是雇主了解求职者情况的一种方式。

sentences.en: What are their strengths and areas in need of development?
sentences.zh: 了解他们的优势以及需要发展的领域。

sentences.en: And that then gets considered with other pieces of information.
sentences.zh: 然后，这些信息会与其他信息综合考量。

sentences.en: And, again, the tenets of fairness apply to all aspects of the application.
sentences.zh: 而且，公平原则同样适用于申请的各个环节。

sentences.en: So, it's not like a test score determines your fate in these systems as much as we might put weight on these scores as we sometimes hear about in the news.
sentences.zh: 所以，测试分数并不会像我们在新闻中偶尔听到的那样，在这些系统中决定你的命运，尽管我们可能会比较看重这些分数。

sentences.en: Whether it's personality, the persona series that you mentioned, or standardized testing in college admissions.
sentences.zh: 无论是你提到的性格测试，还是大学招生中的标准化考试。

sentences.en: No admissions office is relying solely on test scores, I don't imagine.
sentences.zh: 我想，没有哪个招生办公室会仅仅依赖考试成绩。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Less and less.
sentences.zh: 越来越不依赖了。

sentences.en: Yeah, some of them aren't relying on them at all anymore.
sentences.zh: 是的，有些学校已经完全不再依赖这些成绩了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: And that's another conversation to have, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，那是另一个话题了。

sentences.en: So, the last question is kind of a big one.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题比较宏大。

sentences.en: What are the major research questions that you think still need to be answered and what are you studying now?
sentences.zh: 你认为还有哪些重大的研究课题需要解答？你目前正在研究什么？

sentences.en: Wow, that is a big question.
sentences.zh: 哇，这确实是个大问题。

sentences.en: Currently, I've been researching what products are out there in the world of AI and personnel selection,
sentences.zh: 目前，我一直在研究人工智能和人员筛选领域有哪些产品，

sentences.en: what are vendors providing and what evidence is there for their effectiveness.
sentences.zh: 供应商提供了什么，以及有什么证据证明它们的有效性。

sentences.en: And we are, you know, not pretending to engage in fully comprehensive survey of what's out there because it keeps changing even by the day.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有假装在对现有产品进行全面调查，因为它们每天都在变化。

sentences.en: But at least getting a sense of what is being offered,
sentences.zh: 但至少可以了解一下目前提供了什么，

sentences.en: what types of things are being offered and what evidence is out there to support the technologies that are being offered and sold, sometimes at high dollar.
sentences.zh: 提供了哪些类型的产品，以及有什么证据支持这些有时价格昂贵、被推销的技术。

sentences.en: And what do organizations get in return for their investment, what do employers hope to get and how does that align with what they might get from these technologies?
sentences.zh: 企业在投资后能得到什么回报？雇主希望得到什么？这与他们从这些技术中实际获得的东西是否一致？

sentences.en: So, our research is looking there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的研究正着眼于此。

sentences.en: Also, I've been interested in school to work transitions.
sentences.zh: 此外，我也一直对从学校到职场的过渡很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: the question there is whether we can use some forms of detailed data collection or perhaps some machine learning to look at the transitions that people make from their education into the workplace.
sentences.zh: 这里的问题是，我们是否可以使用某种形式的详细数据收集，或者机器学习，来观察人们从教育到职场的过渡。

sentences.en: And it might be a four-year college, it might be a four-year college, it may or may not be a degree, it may be a certification,
sentences.zh: 这可能是一所四年制大学，也可能不是，可能拿到了学位，也可能没有，可能是一个认证，

sentences.en: or people are taking courses relevant to their interests and then getting jobs.
sentences.zh: 或者人们只是在学习与兴趣相关的课程，然后找到工作。

sentences.en: So, what do those transitions look like and how do algorithms capture those regularities so we can understand them?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些过渡是什么样的？算法如何捕捉其中的规律，以便我们能够理解它们？

sentences.en: But then also,
sentences.zh: 但同时，

sentences.en: how can we intervene on that to make sure that people are seeking meaningful employment and steady employment in the world of work in a way that fits their capabilities and also their desires to grow in their field?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何介入，确保人们在职场中寻求到有意义且稳定的工作，既符合他们的能力，也符合他们在各自领域成长的愿望？

sentences.en: Easier said than done, that's a tall order, but we're using data to inform those efforts,
sentences.zh: 说起来容易做起来难，这是一个艰巨的任务，但我们正在利用数据为这些努力提供参考，

sentences.en: but then also connecting with educators and policymakers to see what they do with those findings.
sentences.zh: 同时也与教育工作者和政策制定者沟通，看看他们如何利用这些发现。

sentences.en: So, it's one thing to reflect on the way things have been through the data, but it's another thing then to take that information and say, well, where are we going?
sentences.zh: 通过数据反思过去是一回事，但利用这些信息去思考“我们未来要去向何方”则是另一回事。

sentences.en: What are the new directions that we should be headed in that the data alone don't tell us?
sentences.zh: 我们应该朝着哪些新的方向前进？这是仅凭数据无法告诉我们的。

sentences.en: So, that's been pretty interesting to me and hopefully impactful to a range of folks who, perhaps like me,
sentences.zh: 所以，这对我来说非常有趣，也希望对那些像我一样的人产生影响，

sentences.en: didn't know what they were going to do when they grew up and they kind of fumble their way through the world.
sentences.zh: 他们可能在成长过程中不知道自己要做什么，只能在世界上摸索前行。

sentences.en: You know, I've always been an advocate of even giving a little information can go a long way to open people's eyes to the possibilities.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直主张，即使提供一点点信息，也能在很大程度上开阔人们的视野，让他们看到各种可能性。

sentences.en: Well, this has been very interesting.
sentences.zh: 好的，这非常有意思。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Oswald.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，奥斯瓦尔德博士。

sentences.en: I've enjoyed speaking with you today.
sentences.zh: 今天和您的交谈我很愉快。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you very much, Kim.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你，金。

sentences.en: This has been really great.
sentences.zh: 这真的很棒。

sentences.en: And more importantly, I hope listeners find it interesting and we keep our gears turning on these issues.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，我希望听众们觉得这很有趣，并能让我们继续深入思考这些问题。
